title: Earliest Finish Time for Land and Water Rides II
summary: Given the earliest start times and durations for land and water rides, determine the earliest possible time at which a tourist can finish both rides, with the tourist experiencing exactly one ride from each category in any order.
statement: Given the earliest start times and durations for land and water rides, determine the earliest possible time at which a tourist can finish both rides, with the tourist experiencing exactly one ride from each category in any order. The tourist can start a ride at its earliest start time or any later time, and must wait if the next ride is not yet available.
constraints: Each category has one to 50,000 rides.
Take exactly one ride from each category in either order.
A ride may start at or after its opening time.
hints: For a fixed order, only the earliest possible finish among first-category rides matters.
Compute that finish, then choose the second ride minimizing max(opening,first_finish)+duration.
Evaluate land-water and water-land orders and take the smaller result.
Any later first finish cannot improve a fixed second ride, so the earliest first finish dominates all alternatives.
editorial: Any later first finish cannot improve a fixed second ride, so the earliest first finish dominates all alternatives.

tests.explanation: Land ride zero finishes at six, allowing the water ride to finish at nine.
Taking water first and then land finishes at fourteen.
